title: Tener, estar y decir que no
summary: tener and estar, negation with no, and the first taste of ser vs estar

blocks.title: tener — to have (and more)
blocks.body: **tener** means 'to have', but Spanish also uses it where English uses 'to be': *tener hambre* (to be hungry, lit. 'have hunger'), *tener años* (to be … years old). Learn the set — it's irregular in the first person and stem-changing.

blocks.title: estar — how and where things are
blocks.body: **estar** is the *other* 'to be' — for **location** and **temporary states/feelings**: *estoy en casa* (I'm at home), *estoy cansado* (I'm tired). Ser said who you are (day 4); estar says how you are and where you are right now.

pairs.note: *ser de* = where you're FROM (origin/identity). *estar en* = where you ARE right now (location). We'll go deep on this in week 3.

blocks.title: Saying no — just put 'no' first
blocks.body: Negation is refreshingly simple: put **no** directly **before the verb**. *No tengo hambre* (I'm not hungry). *No estoy en casa* (I'm not home). *No soy de aquí* (I'm not from here). One little *no*, right in front of the verb — that's the whole rule.
blocks.callout: To answer a yes/no question: *No, no tengo…* — the first *no* = 'no', the second is the grammar. Two nos, totally normal.

blocks.explain: Location = **estar**: *estoy en casa*. *Soy en casa* is wrong (ser isn't for location); *tengo casa* means 'I have a house'.

blocks.prompt: Make it negative: 'I'm not tired.' — ___ ___ cansado.
blocks.hint: State/feeling = estar, and *no* goes before the verb.
blocks.explain: *No estoy cansado.* Feeling = estar, and *no* sits right in front of it.

blocks.scene: Rafa checks in with you at the end of a long day

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.en: How's it going? Are you OK?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Estoy un poco cansado, la verdad.

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.en: Are you hungry? There are tapas.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: No, no tengo hambre, gracias. Pero tengo sed.
lines.en: No, I'm not hungry, thanks. But I'm thirsty.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
Write how you feel right now and where you are, using *estar*. Then one thing you have or don't have, using *tener* (try *tengo* / *no tengo*).
